source_review.notes: Checked CNCF's current Platforms White Paper, DORA's corrected 2024 report and platform guidance updated January 12, 2026, Team Topologies, current Backstage Software Templates and Writing Templates documentation, Google's SRE workbook guidance, and NIST SP 800-53 Release 5.2.0. The chapter distinguishes empirical associations, practitioner organization patterns, product documentation, automation guidance, and control catalogs while bounding every tool-specific and current-practice claim.

evidence: Checked road tuple R=(U,J,F,D,C,O,E,L) and defined segments, jobs, predicate, declarations, capabilities, promise, evidence, and lifecycle before reuse.
Checked F:W→{true,false}, route set Q, routing result q(w), and distinction between workload set W and individual workload w.
Checked escape tuple H=(w,r,a,b,o,t,e,z) and every reason, authority, boundary, ownership, time, evidence, and end-state component.
Confirmed all notation uses GitHub-compatible math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The tuples are traceability models and do not claim that road fitness or escape legitimacy reduces to a Boolean or fixed formula.

evidence: Confirmed web-api fits without extension and routes standard.
Confirmed tracing-plugin fits with extension and routes extension.
Confirmed gpu-batch selects alternate before escape, confidential-runtime selects approved escape, and clinical-controller defaults independent.
Recomputed one occurrence for each of the five ordered route labels and matched counts=1,1,1,1,1.
Confirmed all six stdout lines exactly match the snippet annotation and generated report.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Inputs are synthetic flags; counts are not estimates of real portfolio fit, demand, safety, or approval quality.

evidence: Traced road completeness from eligible segments and jobs through fitness, declarations, capabilities, promises, evidence, and lifecycle.
Checked that F(w)=false does not entail escape because alternate and independent routes remain possible.
Checked that leaving road defaults does not entail waiver of cross-cutting obligations.
Checked that unchanged generated text does not entail conformance when dependencies or assumptions drift, and textual difference does not entail nonconformance when invariants hold.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic review establishes distinctions and non-entailments rather than a formal optimal-routing theorem.

evidence: Reviewed standard, bounded configuration, extension, alternate, temporary escape, emergency escape, permanent independent, re-entry, deprecated, and retired paths.
Reviewed novice, expert, influential, unsupported, regulated, experimental, remote, accessible, low-use high-consequence, and affected-party contexts.
Reviewed mandatory adoption, denied escape, secret bypass, plugin risk, provider leakage, generated drift, auto-upgrade blast radius, version proliferation, controller outage, and shadow work.
Reviewed clinical controller and government analytics cases with regulatory, clinical, legal, privacy, incident-command, data-steward, accessibility, operator, and community authorities.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Regulatory, clinical, public-policy, legal, privacy, and affected-community acceptance remain outside unilateral platform authority.

evidence: Checked eligibility follows workload evidence rather than team rank or organizational influence.
Checked domain authority and consequential assumptions remain visible across defaults, extensions, alternates, escapes, and independent paths.
Checked operational completeness through support, observability, dependencies, compatibility, upgrade, incident, migration, deprecation, and retirement.
Checked obligation continuity and explicit transfer of build, operation, security, cost, incident, migration, and retirement ownership.
Checked recorded escapes and deviations feed product-scope review rather than automatic punishment or productization.
invariant_checking.notes: Each implemented road and extension still needs technology-specific conformance, security, reliability, accessibility, migration, and consumer evidence.

evidence: Reviewed mandatory adoption plus delayed escape as a counterexample disproving that adoption percentage entails workload fitness.
Reviewed copy-time scaffolding as a counterexample disproving that a current template entails a maintained road.
Reviewed a permanent undocumented executive exemption as a counterexample distinguishing bypass from governed escape.
Reviewed the clinical controller as a counterexample to universal-road claims while preserving shared capability value.
Confirmed the executable model proves only classification for declared synthetic flags.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides bounded routing arguments and falsifying cases, not formal proof that a road is optimal, safe, or attractive.

evidence: Audited uses of paved, golden, preferred, fit, safe, secure, supported, conformant, optional, attractive, best, valid, and evidence.
Confirmed road quality claims are bounded by archetype, context, contract, authority, lifecycle, and observed outcomes.
Confirmed source guidance, adoption, conformance, template execution, and internal approval are not labeled as universal correctness proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The word golden is explicitly treated as a hypothesis rather than objective superiority.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/PLAT-006/report.json records exact execution of road-routing-model under the captured Python 3 toolchain.
Reproduced standard, extension, alternate, escape, and independent outcomes with one count each.
Confirmed the chapter denies real fitness, authority, technical feasibility, risk, support capacity, consumer acceptance, or approval quality from the artifact.
Confirmed product measurement guidance qualifies eligibility, mandates, rejected and abandoned escapes, drift, recovery, migration, harms, and platform burden.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution verifies the stated pure routing rule only; no production or human-subject evidence is represented.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed paved road versus template/tool/standard, road tuple and workload archetypes, decision categories, meaningful declarations, five routing outcomes, escape records, extensions, scaffolding drift, attractiveness, versioning, lifecycle, and fit measurement. The chapter keeps escape distinct from waiver and bypass and independent ownership distinct from product failure.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed repository templates, telemetry extensions, GPU batch alternates, confidential-runtime experiments, executive bypasses, generated-instance updates, mandatory adoption, direct cloud services, emergency rollback, clinical controllers, dependency updates, reconciliation, migrations, incident roles, and cost ownership. Every route includes explicit support and lifecycle consequences.

pedagogical_review.notes: The objectives align with ten distinct examples and five exercises progressing from road-completeness retrieval through classification, escape design, lifecycle mechanism comparison, and government analytics transfer. Each answer supplies a complete model with assumptions and authority boundaries.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
